main_body: Round stone well: a light grey stone rim ring around a dark water opening, on a block-built stone front wall, with a wooden beam on two posts above.
top_band: Light grey stone rim, rows 14-15 (L 169-206) at the back, closing into a lip at rows 22-24 (L 97) at the front. The water ellipse sits between them (rows 16-21).
evidence: The column at x=16 reads the back rim (light, rows 14-15), then a dark outline at row 16, then dark blue water at rows 17-21. This is an elliptical opening seen from above. Below it comes the front stone lip (rows 22-24), then a darker shadow row (25-26), then the block-built front wall down to row 31. The opening is clearly visible as an ellipse with highlights on the water, and the ring is wider than the posts. This matches the green container/barrel guide. The front wall is stone courses rather than recessed panels, so recessed_front is false, which is fine for a well. The wooden frame is only a secondary part and is drawn correctly.

style.evidence: The stone ramp has about 6 steps (#c9d1d0, #9eadad, #74888a, #576568, #404a4e, #2b3236), plus a separate water ramp and 3-4 wood tones, which matches the references. Flat-fill coverage is 0%, the same as the roofed well reference. The near-neutral dark edge share is 27%, close to the roofed well's 33%, so the outline is partly tinted rather than a uniform black sticker line. Stones are shaded block by block with highlights. Colour count (23 against 38-40) and colours per tile (11 against 17-20) are lower than both references, so the piece is somewhat thinner, but not enough to look flat or sticker-like beside them.
